fort.name: Sinhagad
fort.note: approximate, tier T3; refine from survey

landmarks.name: Pune Darwaza
landmarks.alt_names: Pune Gate; Pune Darwaja; three successive gates (Pune Gate 1, 2, 3)
landmarks.location_description: North-east side of the fort. First entrance met by visitors coming from the parking area beside the sheer Khadakada cliff (S01, S02, S04).
landmarks.materials: Stone masonry (type not stated; local basalt of the Sahyadri is expected: ESTIMATE, confirm on site). Repaired sections are visibly different in finish.
landmarks.dates: Original date unknown. Gate 3 considered the oldest main entrance by S02. Repairs on gate 2 are extensive (date unknown).

components.name: Gate 1 (outer)
components.description: Built between two bastions on the cliff edge. Weathered, but two carved sharabha (mythical creatures) are still visible on it.

components.name: Stair between gate 1 and gate 2
components.description: About 20 to 25 steps.

components.name: Rock-cut cistern at cliff
components.description: On the left, just before gate 2. Water stagnant and covered with algae.

components.name: Rampart and postern
components.description: From the stair, the fort wall runs down the slope towards gate 1, with a small postern gate set in the rampart. It leads into the detached Khadakada cliff section (see Other remains).

components.name: Gate 2 (middle)
components.description: Also built between two bastions. Heavily repaired, so no carvings remain visible. Steps lead up to the bastion and gate structures.

components.name: Gate 3 (inner)
components.description: Short distance further, again between two bastions. The doorway has a lotus motif and a festoon carving; the source suggests this was the original main entrance.

components.name: Guard rooms
components.description: Visible on either side of the gates.

components.name: Siting
components.description: Each gate sits where a cliff is on one side and a steep valley on the other.

appearance_notes: Sequence of three stone gateways climbing a slope, each flanked by two bastions, with a cliff on one side and a drop on the other.
Gate 1: weathered stone with two sharabha carvings. Gate 2: plain, repaired masonry. Gate 3: lotus and festoon carving at the doorway.
modelling_instructions: Build as three separate gate assemblies (PD_G1, PD_G2, PD_G3) on one continuous ascending approach.
Each gate: two flanking bastions + gate passage + guard rooms on both sides. Use photos PH01, PH10, PH15, PH17 to set proportions and arch shape.
G1: add two weathered low-relief sharabha. G3: add lotus and festoon in the doorway. G2: plain repaired masonry, no carving.
Add the 20-25 step stair between G1 and G2 and the rock-cut cistern on the cliff side.
Blend the footings into the terrain mesh; the gates are defined by the cliff on one side and the valley on the other.
landmarks.collision: Passage floor, stair treads, bastion and wall solids; keep the passage walkable. Postern as a separate opening.

Exact shape and style of the sharabha reliefs
Interior of guard rooms and upper chambers

Measure passage width and height, step riser and tread
Close-ups of sharabha, lotus and festoon carving

landmarks.name: Kalyan Darwaza
landmarks.alt_names: Kalyan Gate; Kalyan Darwaja; Konkan Gate
landmarks.location_description: South-east side of the fort. Second official entrance, used by people approaching from Kondhanpur (S01, S02).
landmarks.materials: Stone masonry (type not stated; ESTIMATE basalt, confirm).
landmarks.dates: Gate built or repaired Shaka 1672 (about 1750 CE) per inscription; earlier origin possible.

components.name: Two successive gates
components.description: Two gates, each between bastions, with the whole section enclosed by fortified walls arranged like a battle formation.

components.name: Stair between gates
components.description: About 20 to 25 steep steps from the first gate to the second.

components.name: First gate arch
components.description: Carved with two lotus flowers; the festoon above them is damaged.

components.name: Guardroom
components.description: A small guardroom inside the wall near the gate.

components.name: Inscription
components.description: Carved in the arch: the gate was built or repaired in the time of Nanasaheb Peshwa, year Shalivahan Shaka 1672 (about 1750 CE), naming Shrimant Balaji Bajirao Peshwa.

components.name: Bastion reliefs
components.description: One bastion has a boar carving; the opposite bastion has a relief of a mahout riding an elephant.

components.name: Interior ramparts
components.description: Soldiers' quarters in the interior ramparts near the gate.

components.name: Inner approach
components.description: A straight staircase leads into the fort interior; a path along the ramparts leads to the next bastion (Tehalni Buruj).

appearance_notes: Compact fortified gateway complex of two gates in a rising, enclosed approach.
Lotus-carved arch at the first gate with a damaged festoon above; boar relief on one bastion, mahout and elephant on the other.

Bastion reliefs: boar on one, mahout on an elephant on the opposite one, from PH02, PH16, PH17.
Add the small guardroom, soldiers' quarters in the interior rampart, and the straight staircase into the fort.
Connect to the rampart walk and the Tehalni Buruj (see Bastions).

landmarks.name: Fortification walls
landmarks.alt_names: Ramparts; tofa; fortification; Khadakada enclosure walls
landmarks.location_description: Walls and bastions are built only at key places because the steep slopes give natural protection (S01). Ramparts run beside the Khadakada cliff near the parking area, descend beside the third Pune gate, and form a walkable rampart route around the fort (S02).
landmarks.materials: Stone masonry; some restored sections. Wall type and mortar not documented.
landmarks.dates: Mixed, many repair phases. Unknown per segment.

components.name: Cliff-side rampart near parking
components.description: A rampart runs along the sheer Khadakada cliff next to the approach.

components.name: Khadakada enclosure
components.description: A slightly detached cliff section enclosed by its own independent ramparts and bastions, with a small gate and a higher small gate to the upper part.

components.name: Rampart descending beside Daru Kothar
components.description: A rampart descends beside the gunpowder storehouse after gate 3.

components.name: Water channel through rampart
components.description: A water channel shaped like a miniature doorway carries water through the rampart near the Kalyan route.

components.name: Interior rampart near Kalyan gate
components.description: Contains soldiers' quarters.

components.name: Cliff-edge rampart near Rajaram samadhi
components.description: Five underground rock-cut cisterns lie near the cliff-edge rampart.

components.name: Dongiri cliff / Tanaji Kada
components.description: The rampart edge historically called Dongiri cliff, now popularly Tanaji Kada, is the cliff where Tanaji's force is said to have climbed.

components.name: Overall
components.description: Walls were built at key places only; much of the perimeter relies on the cliff.

appearance_notes: Stone ramparts on a cliff top, with long stretches where the natural cliff replaces a wall.
Water channels cut through the wall; gates and posterns in the ramparts.

Use a placeholder wall profile only until measured; flag as T3.

landmarks.name: Defensive bastions
landmarks.location_description: Along the rampart: flanking all gates, on spurs, and at corners (S02). Buruj join the walls, strengthen them and act as watch towers or gun bases (S16, general).
landmarks.tier_target: T3 until each bastion is photographed

components.name: Gate bastions
components.description: Each of the three Pune gates and two Kalyan gates sits between two bastions.

components.name: Khadakada spur bastion
components.description: A large bastion on a spur from the main fort overlooks the Khadakada section.

components.name: Ruined bastion near TV tower
components.description: Large bastion at the fort edge beyond the Doordarshan tower; ruined and awaiting restoration; wide view of Khadakada and parking.

components.name: Tehalni Buruj (Watch Bastion)
components.description: Built to monitor the Kalyan gate route. A rock-cut cistern lies above it on a slope.

components.name: Zunjar Buruj
components.description: At the southern edge on a spur cut off from the ridge. The steps up to it are buried; a partly exposed latrine pit is visible; a shallow dry tank is nearby; a hidden escape route descends to Kalki Met.

components.name: Large outer bastion beyond Zunjar
components.description: Another large bastion built outside the main rampart.

components.name: Bastion opposite Daru Kothar
components.description: Holds a 6-foot cannon on a cart brought from Moradari village; inscribed with Marathi text reading 'Gumabh' and the number 248.

components.name: Named bastions (lead only)
components.description: A student study lists Khadkadyacha, Kalavanti, Aale, Yashwant, Dalkathicha and Zunjar burj. Not confirmed.

appearance_notes: Rounded or angular stone bastions projecting from the rampart at gates, spurs and cliff corners, some ruined, some restored.

landmarks.location_description: On the rampart walk after Tanaji Kada and before the pond and cliff-edge cisterns near Rajaram's samadhi. Just before it a secret path descends to the Amri Met outpost (S02).

components.name: Bastion
components.description: A named bastion along the rampart edge.

components.name: Secret path

components.name: Pond

components.name: Cisterns

landmarks.name: Daru Kothar
landmarks.location_description: Immediately to the right after passing through the third Pune gate, beside the descending rampart (S02).
landmarks.dates: Original unknown; damaged and repaired after 1751; used as a church in British times (dates unknown).

components.name: Building
components.description: Stone-built storehouse, remarkably well preserved today.

components.name: Explosion
components.description: Lightning struck it on 11 September 1751; the explosion destroyed the adjacent Fadnis residence and killed its occupants. Repairs to the storehouse and surroundings later cost 8,700 rupees.

components.name: British period use
components.description: Briefly converted into a church.

components.name: Drain
components.description: A stone channel carved into the wall drains water. Fragments of old temple carvings are embedded in it.

appearance_notes: Solid stone storehouse, intact, with a carved stone drain channel in the wall that includes reused temple carving fragments.
modelling_instructions: Model the exterior from photographs only. Interior only if photographed.
Show repair phases as subtle material change (post-1751). Include the stone drain channel with embedded carved fragments.
Do not add Christian church features (windows, cross, tower) unless photos show them.

landmarks.name: Kondhaneshwar / Kaundinyeshwar Temple
landmarks.location_description: Reached by steps climbing from the Tanaji memorial. Behind it is the highest point of the fort (Gadmatha), 4,314 ft (S02).
landmarks.dates: Ancient, exact date UNKNOWN. Do not label it Hemadpanti or any style unless a source states it.

components.name: Shrine
components.description: Ancient shrine with worn door jambs that indicate its age.

components.name: Interior
components.description: Contains a Shiva lingam and a Ganesha idol.

components.name: Courtyard
components.description: A Nandi and a stone lamp tower (deepmala).

components.name: Highest point
components.description: Behind the temple is the fort's summit (Gadmatha).

components.name: Antiquity clue
components.description: Temple carvings and caves suggest the fort could be about 2,000 years old; Satavahana-period caves for water storage and temple carvings are mentioned.

appearance_notes: Small ancient stone shrine with worn carved door frames, a Nandi and a stone deepmala in the courtyard, set near the summit.

components.name: Platform

components.name: Hathi Talav

landmarks.dates: Original memorial believed about 350 years old (S01, S06). Later phases 1938, 1941, 1976; restoration discovered 2019.

landmarks.name: Other documented historical remains
landmarks.alt_names: Horse stables, commandant's mansion, shrines, memorials, Khadakada, etc.

components.description: Not a stable but a partly excavated ancient cave complex with pillars and a veranda. Eight cisterns have formed in it; holes in the outer rock show where wooden roof pillars may have stood. A cistern is in front; three smaller unfinished caves further on, also water-filled.

components.name: Lost buildings
components.description: Jawahir Khana, Ratna Shala and Rajwada were listed in an 1876 advertisement; no remains described. Do not model.

appearance_notes: Caves with pillars and verandah (horse stables), ruined mansion arches, small domed shrines, memorial platforms, a sati-stone dome.
modelling_instructions: Make each item a separate asset with its own record. Start with the Horse Stables (best documented), then the commandant's mansion remains, shrines and memorials.
Do not rebuild lost buildings. Leave ruins as ruins.
TV tower is optional and modern: add it last if visible from walking routes.
landmarks.collision: Per asset; cave floors walkable; ruins as solid mass with gaps only where visible.
